source.title: Neural Networks Asymptotic Behaviours for the Resolution of Inverse Problems
source.authors: L. Del Debbio; M. Naviglio; Francesco Tarantelli

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies neural-network asymptotics for a toy inverse problem. It reports width-dependent reconstruction accuracy, not training classification error or the conditions named in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports finite-width MLP reconstruction results and their convergence toward Gaussian-process results as width increases. These use a toy harmonic-oscillator inverse problem and do not measure the training classification behavior in the claim versions. CIFAR-10 and MNIST are mentioned only as prior work.
record.test_reason: The study measures spectral-density reconstruction by finite-width MLPs and their Gaussian-process limits. It reports no results on the classification error, teacher-student minima, depth degradation, initialization comparisons, stability-threshold dynamics or normalization effects named in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: both GP limits outperform the finite-width MLP on this toy inverse problem, and the MLP approaches their accuracy as width increases. The authors suggest finite-width parameter nonlinearities may be unnecessary here and explicitly require further investigation before generalizing.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains an MLP with MSE and gradient descent for a toy inverse problem; it does not use the classification benchmarks or error measure in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer width changes the reconstruction output; the paper reports that finite-width NN results approach GP results as width increases.

fits_no_version.finding: On the harmonic-oscillator inverse problem, both GP limits outperform the finite-width MLP, and increasing MLP width makes its reconstruction approach the GP results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this inverse-problem task and training recipe, wider MLPs approach the spectral-reconstruction accuracy of their Gaussian-process limits.

record.problems: The numerical task is a toy harmonic-oscillator inverse problem, and the authors caution against generalizing the results. Width-dependent outcomes are shown in a figure without numerical accuracy values. The paper itself says finite-width NN training relies on stopping conditions and does not reach the absolute loss minimum.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and effects of size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on excess student width.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and the special initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above initial stability limits, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The discussion of finite-width stopping criteria supplies no measured training-error result and does not challenge V1. The learning-rate bound in Section 2C is attributed to prior work and does not test V5. Citations to initialization and deep-network papers do not constitute tests of their claims.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, training duration, early stopping and regularization effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects on classification training error, identity shortcuts, special initialization and normalization.
Initialization effects on signal or gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, loss rises, curvature or sharpness during training, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained with MSE loss and gradient descent on the stated inverse-problem training set; compared with asymptotic GP methods.
rows.measure: Spectral-density reconstruction accuracy relative to the GP results; plotted outcome, no numeric accuracy stated.
rows.uncertainty: Bootstrap resampling is used for final uncertainties; no numeric uncertainty stated for this width comparison.
rows.note: This is reconstruction accuracy for a toy inverse problem, not training classification error.
rows.check: The outcome is test-point spectral reconstruction, not an effect named by any version. The comparison references are NNGP and NTK-GP outputs; the baseline should not be 'not stated'.
